what_it_is: Rule, not a fixed path. A project is a folder holding .git, package.json, Cargo.toml, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, composer.json, Gemfile, go.mod, pubspec.yaml or an .xcodeproj. Searched under ~/Development, ~/Projects, ~/Documents, ~/Desktop, ~/Sites (Mac) or ~/source/repos (Windows), and any extra disk you choose, down to three folder levels.

what_it_is: Rule, not a fixed path. what_it_is: Rule, not a path. In repositories found by the project search, old backup refs left by git filter-branch (refs/original/*) and a refs/stash that has no stashes behind it. They keep unreachable history alive and make .git larger than it needs to be.

path: ~/Library/{Application Support, Caches, Containers, HTTPStorages, Saved Application State, Logs}/<bundle id>
what_it_is: Rule, not a fixed path. Entries in those six folders whose name looks like a bundle identifier (at least two dots) and that no installed app owns, 1 MB or larger. Names starting com.apple., group.com.apple., apple., com.google., google., com.microsoft., com.adobe., org.mozilla., com.docker., com.electron., com.github. or io.tauri. are never judged. Installed apps are matched by bundle id, then by app name. Entries are marked confirmed when the owning app is not running, otherwise review.
safe_to_delete_because: Nothing installed owns them. Only entries marked confirmed are ticked by default; the folders themselves are never ticked as a group. They go to the Trash, so a wrong call can be undone.
cost_of_deleting: an app you reinstall starts with fresh settings

what_it_is: Rule, not a fixed path. Top-level folders in AppData Roaming and Local, 1 MB or larger, whose name matches no installed program listed in the registry's uninstall keys and is not on a built-in allow-list of shared vendors (for example Microsoft, Windows, Google, Adobe, NVIDIA, Docker, JetBrains, Python, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic).
safe_to_delete_because: Nothing installed appears to own them. Because this is a judgement call, all of these are marked review and none is ticked. They go to the Recycle Bin.
cost_of_deleting: an app you reinstall starts with fresh settings
check_command_windows: Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA","$env:LOCALAPPDATA" -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { "$($_.FullName) : " + ((Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum / 1GB) }

what_it_is: Rule, not a fixed path. Microsoft Store app data folders of 1 MB or more whose package is not in the list of installed Store apps. Nothing is offered if that list could not be read.
safe_to_delete_because: The package is no longer installed. Entries are marked confirmed and ticked by default. They go to the Recycle Bin.
cost_of_deleting: an app you reinstall starts with fresh settings

what_it_is: Rule. Your own login-item files whose program is an absolute path that no longer exists. Labels starting com.apple. are skipped, symlinks are skipped, and a program on /Volumes (which may just be unplugged) never counts as missing.
safe_to_delete_because: The program it launches is provably gone, so the entry can only fail. An app that still wants it recreates it. The file goes to the Trash.
cost_of_deleting: nothing; the entry is recreated if the app wants it

what_it_is: Rule. Your own start-at-sign-in entries (current user only) whose program is an absolute path that no longer exists. Names without a full path, such as rundll32.exe, and programs on drives or network shares that are not present are never judged.
safe_to_delete_because: The program is provably gone. Prune first saves a .reg backup of the value and moves it to the Recycle Bin, so double-clicking it restores the entry.
cost_of_deleting: nothing; the entry can be restored from the backup

what_it_is: Backups Finder made of your iPhone or iPad, often several GB each. The newest backup of each device is badged 'Latest for this device'.
safe_to_delete_because: Older backups are usually safe if the device has a newer backup, for example in iCloud. Never ticked, so you decide per backup. They go to the Trash.
cost_of_deleting: that backup can no longer be restored from

what_it_is: iOS and iPadOS installer files Finder downloaded to update a device.
safe_to_delete_because: Safe once the device is updated; Finder downloads a new one if an update needs it.
cost_of_deleting: re-downloads if you need it again

what_it_is: Full macOS installer apps, usually 12 GB or more. Only the app bundle itself, and only when its bundle id starts with com.apple.InstallAssistant, is accepted.
safe_to_delete_because: Safe unless you plan to install that macOS version. This is the one place outside your home folder where Prune can remove an app. Never ticked; goes to the Trash.
cost_of_deleting: re-download from the App Store if needed

path: ~/Downloads, ~/Desktop, ~/Documents (and OneDrive Desktop and Documents on Windows) - files of 100 MB or more (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, %USERPROFILE%\Desktop, %USERPROFILE%\Documents (and OneDrive Desktop and Documents) - files of 100 MB or more)
what_it_is: Rule, not a cache. Single files of 100 MB or more, found up to four folders deep. Hidden folders, the Library or AppData folder, and on Mac the CloudStorage and Mobile Documents folders are never walked. Listed for you to review one by one.
safe_to_delete_because: These are your own files, so they are never safe by default: nothing about them is regenerable. They are listed only so you can see what is big. Never ticked; goes to the Trash or Recycle Bin.
cost_of_deleting: permanent unless restored from the Trash or Recycle Bin
check_command_windows: Get-ChildItem "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads","$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop","$env:USERPROFILE\Documents" -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Length -gt 100MB | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object FullName,@{n="GB";e={$_.Length/1GB}}

path: same folders as Large files - files of 50 to 100 MB not opened or changed for about 6 months
what_it_is: Rule, not a cache. Files between 50 MB and 100 MB whose last-used time (the later of last opened and last changed) is older than 183 days.
safe_to_delete_because: Age alone cannot show that a file is unwanted, so these are only shown. Never ticked; goes to the Trash or Recycle Bin.
cost_of_deleting: permanent unless restored from the Trash or Recycle Bin

path: ~/Downloads - files under 50 MB not opened for 3 months or more
what_it_is: Rule, not a cache. Small files in Downloads (hidden files skipped) grouped by how long since they were last used: 3-12 months, 1-2 years, 2+ years. Anything used in the last 90 days is never listed.
safe_to_delete_because: These are your own documents and cannot be regenerated, so the groups are shown for review only. Never ticked; goes to the Trash or Recycle Bin.
cost_of_deleting: permanent unless restored from the Trash or Recycle Bin

what_it_is: Rule. The same model weights (100 MB or more) sitting in two or more of Ollama, Hugging Face and LM Studio stores. Ollama and Hugging Face files are matched by the SHA-256 name they already carry; others are compared by size, then a 1 MB head hash, then a full hash. Symlinks and hard-linked files are never candidates.
safe_to_delete_because: Keep one copy and remove the rest. The review screen refuses to remove every copy of a set. Removing the Ollama copy also removes the Ollama models that use it; removing a Hugging Face copy means it downloads again if a script asks. Never ticked; goes to the Trash or Recycle Bin.
cost_of_deleting: model re-downloads if a tool asks for it again

path: ~/Downloads, ~/Desktop, ~/Documents - identical files of 10 MB or more
what_it_is: Rule. Byte-identical files of 10 MB or more in the same three folders, up to six folders deep. App-style packages (.app, .bundle, .framework, .photoslibrary and similar) are not looked inside.
safe_to_delete_because: You choose which copy to keep; nothing is ticked and the screen refuses to remove every copy. Goes to the Trash or Recycle Bin.
cost_of_deleting: none, if one copy is kept
check_command_windows: Get-ChildItem "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads","$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop","$env:USERPROFILE\Documents" -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Length -gt 10MB | Get-FileHash | Group-Object Hash | Where-Object Count -gt 1
